1	# Resurrection Review — kids-drawing-app
2	
3	**Session:** `resurrect-20260521`
4	**Date:** 2026-05-21
5	**Branch audited:** `main` (HEAD `e973b76`)
6	**Method:** 6 parallel scientist audits (inventory, functionality, UX/a11y, testing, quality/deps, variety/vision) + 1 cross-validation pass. All findings ground-truthed against source on `main`.
7	
8	> This report is structured to be consumed by `/ralplan`. Each finding is atomic, severity-tagged, evidence-linked, and grouped so phases can be cut without re-deriving scope. **Nothing has been implemented.**
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 0. The 30-second read
13	
14	- **The bones are healthy.** TS strict on, 0 `any`, 0 ESLint issues, build green in 1s, gzipped JS ~94 KB. No production CVEs. The codebase is in better shape than agent-grown projects usually are.
15	- **The product has drifted.** Docs (README/SPECIFICATIONS/CLAUDE.md) still describe a *drawing app* with AI stencils + Firebase + PWA. Reality is a *games hub*: 13 games on `main`, drawing exists but **the save button is a `console.log` stub** while the UI says "✨ Your drawing will be automatically saved!". The first decision is whether to honor the original identity or rename to match reality.
16	- **CI is red and nobody noticed.** 14 of 86 unit tests fail on `main` (localStorage not polyfilled in jsdom setup). `npm run test:touch` references a `vitest.mobile.config.ts` that has never existed. Mandated `lighthouse:mobile` not in CI.
17	- **There is a large "shadow inventory."** 6 complete arcade games (Flappy Bird, Breakout, Pac-Man, Space Invaders, Pong, Endless Runner) + 1 WIP (Bubble Shooter) all live on a single never-merged branch. DotPath is a separate open PR. Triage of these is its own sub-project.
18	- **Only two true Blockers** survive after re-tiering: the red test suite (T2/T3) and JellyVolleyball's broken touch coordinates on phones (U5). Everything else is missing-features or polish.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## 1. Identity Decision (gate before anything else)
23	
24	The project must pick a direction before the resurrection plan can be sequenced. Stage 6 framed three options:
25	
26	| Option | What it is | Pros | Cons |
27	|---|---|---|---|
28	| **A. Re-focus on drawing** | Trim/freeze games. Build gallery, AI stencils, Firebase, PWA per SPECIFICATIONS.MD. | Honors original identity. Differentiated (few good kids drawing PWAs). | 13 implemented games become sunk cost. AI + Firebase = real money. |
29	| **B. Embrace "kids' learning hub"** ★ | Drawing + games coexist. Restore drawing credibility *first* (gallery + daily prompt) so the app's name stops lying. | Lowest disruption. Most content already shipped. Broad age coverage (3-8). | Identity is diffuse. Homepage of 13+ tiles becoming unwieldy. |
30	| **C. Split into two apps** | Drawing app and games app become separate repos. | Clean identities. | 2× maintenance. Premature at current scale. |
31	
32	**Recommendation (Stage 6 + verifier concur): Option B**, conditional on completing the Drawing Gallery + Daily Prompt items in Phase 1 below. Option A becomes viable later if owner commits to AI stencil + Firebase work. Option C deferred.
33	
34	> `ralplan` should treat this as a **user-gated decision**. The phases below assume B; A and C require re-scoping.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 2. Resurrection Phasing (ordered for `/ralplan`)
39	
40	### Phase 0 — Make CI honest (1–2 days, must precede everything)
41	
42	| # | Action | Source finding | Severity |
43	|---|---|---|---|
44	| 0.1 | Add `localStorage` polyfill in `src/test/setup.ts` (e.g. `import 'jest-localstorage-mock'` or a hand-rolled stub). Fixes 14 failing tests in one line. | T2, T3 | **Blocker** |
45	| 0.2 | Create the missing `vitest.mobile.config.ts` *or* remove `test:touch` from `package.json`. Currently the script always exits 1. | T6 | **Blocker** |
46	| 0.3 | Add `test-results/` to `.gitignore`; un-track the committed `test-results/` and `dist/` and `svg/` dirs. | I7, T7 | Minor |
47	| 0.4 | Wire `test:games`, `test:e2e`, `lint`, and `lighthouse:mobile` into `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Currently CI only runs the broken `vitest` step. | T5 | Major |
48	| 0.5 | Add a `webServer` stanza to `playwright.config.ts` so e2e can actually run in CI. | T7 | Major |
49	
50	**Why Phase 0:** every later phase needs green CI to land safely. Skipping this turns Phase 1 into "is my new code broken or was it always broken?"
51	
52	### Phase 1 — Restore identity credibility (S-effort, 3–5 days)
53

55	|---|---|---|---|
56	| 1.1 | **Wire up Drawing save → localStorage with the `SavedDrawing` interface from SPECIFICATIONS.MD.** Replace the `console.log` stub in `DrawingPage.tsx:16-19`. The footer text "Your drawing will be automatically saved!" is currently a lie. | F2, V2#1 | **Major** |

# Resurrection Review — kids-drawing-app

**Session:** `resurrect-20260521`
**Date:** 2026-05-21
**Branch audited:** `main` (HEAD `e973b76`)
**Method:** 6 parallel scientist audits (inventory, functionality, UX/a11y, testing, quality/deps, variety/vision) + 1 cross-validation pass. All findings ground-truthed against source on `main`.

> This report is structured to be consumed by `/ralplan`. Each finding is atomic, severity-tagged, evidence-linked, and grouped so phases can be cut without re-deriving scope. **Nothing has been implemented.**

---

## 0. The 30-second read

- **The bones are healthy.** TS strict on, 0 `any`, 0 ESLint issues, build green in 1s, gzipped JS ~94 KB. No production CVEs. The codebase is in better shape than agent-grown projects usually are.
- **The product has drifted.** Docs (README/SPECIFICATIONS/CLAUDE.md) still describe a *drawing app* with AI stencils + Firebase + PWA. Reality is a *games hub*: 13 games on `main`, drawing exists but **the save button is a `console.log` stub** while the UI says "✨ Your drawing will be automatically saved!". The first decision is whether to honor the original identity or rename to match reality.
- **CI is red and nobody noticed.** 14 of 86 unit tests fail on `main` (localStorage not polyfilled in jsdom setup). `npm run test:touch` references a `vitest.mobile.config.ts` that has never existed. Mandated `lighthouse:mobile` not in CI.
- **There is a large "shadow inventory."** 6 complete arcade games (Flappy Bird, Breakout, Pac-Man, Space Invaders, Pong, Endless Runner) + 1 WIP (Bubble Shooter) all live on a single never-merged branch. DotPath is a separate open PR. Triage of these is its own sub-project.
- **Only two true Blockers** survive after re-tiering: the red test suite (T2/T3) and JellyVolleyball's broken touch coordinates on phones (U5). Everything else is missing-features or polish.

---

## 1. Identity Decision (gate before anything else)

The project must pick a direction before the resurrection plan can be sequenced. Stage 6 framed three options:

| Option | What it is | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Re-focus on drawing** | Trim/freeze games. Build gallery, AI stencils, Firebase, PWA per SPECIFICATIONS.MD. | Honors original identity. Differentiated (few good kids drawing PWAs). | 13 implemented games become sunk cost. AI + Firebase = real money. |
| **B. Embrace "kids' learning hub"** ★ | Drawing + games coexist. Restore drawing credibility *first* (gallery + daily prompt) so the app's name stops lying. | Lowest disruption. Most content already shipped. Broad age coverage (3-8). | Identity is diffuse. Homepage of 13+ tiles becoming unwieldy. |
| **C. Split into two apps** | Drawing app and games app become separate repos. | Clean identities. | 2× maintenance. Premature at current scale. |

**Recommendation (Stage 6 + verifier concur): Option B**, conditional on completing the Drawing Gallery + Daily Prompt items in Phase 1 below. Option A becomes viable later if owner commits to AI stencil + Firebase work. Option C deferred.

> `ralplan` should treat this as a **user-gated decision**. The phases below assume B; A and C require re-scoping.

---

## 2. Resurrection Phasing (ordered for `/ralplan`)

### Phase 0 — Make CI honest (1–2 days, must precede everything)

| # | Action | Source finding | Severity |

| 0.2 | Create the missing `vitest.mobile.config.ts` *or* remove `test:touch` from `package.json`. Currently the script always exits 1. | T6 | **Blocker** |

# Plan — kids-drawing-app Resurrection
**Status:** Draft v1 (Planner) — awaiting Architect review (Gemini)
**Source:** `.omc/research/resurrect-20260521/report.md`
**Branch baseline:** `main` @ `e973b76`
**Mode:** short RALPLAN-DR (no `--deliberate`)

---

## RALPLAN-DR Summary

### Principles (in priority order)
1. **Restore trust before adding features.** Green CI and an honest drawing-save loop come before anything new. The product currently lies to the user ("automatically saved!" while doing nothing) and to its CI ("tests pass" while 14 fail). Trust is the precondition for every other improvement.
2. **Small, reversible PRs.** Resurrection means re-engaging cognitive load on a stale repo. Every PR should be reviewable in <30 min and revertable in <5 min. No multi-week branches.
3. **One blast-radius-large refactor at a time.** Router migration, dep upgrades, and game-shell standardization each touch many files. They cannot land in the same week without thrashing review and breaking bisect.
4. **Defer scope, don't expand it.** The audit produced ~50 findings and a 10-game variety menu. The resurrection sprint commits to the first 4 phases (~30 items). Everything else (Phase 6 features, Phase 7 hygiene, the arcade-branch triage) becomes a roadmap document, not a sprint task.
5. **Honor the primary user.** The dev's daughter — likely ages 4–8 — is the only real user. Optimize for her: large touch targets, mobile-first, no-text difficulty, undo/restart prominence. Accessibility for screen readers etc. is also worth doing, but the priority is the kid playing on the phone.

### Decision Drivers (top 3)
1. **Time-to-honest-product.** How fast can the user re-engage the repo with confidence that what's shipped matches what's promised? Drives the placement of Phases 0–1 first.
2. **Safe rate of change.** This is a one-developer project that's been dormant. The plan must be paceable by one human, with reverts trivially possible. Drives small-PR principle and the dep-upgrade quarantine.
3. **Identity ambiguity unresolved.** Whether to commit to drawing-app, games-hub, or hybrid is a strategic decision the planner cannot make. Drives the **Identity Gate** at the very top of execution.

### Viable Options

**Option A — Sequential phased sprint (this plan's recommendation)**
Run Phases 0 → 1 → 2 → 3a (small) → 5 → 3b (router) → 4 in order, each phase landing as a small PR (or PR series) with green CI before the next phase opens. ~6 weeks at a comfortable pace for one developer.
*Pros:* Each PR is small and revertable. CI stays green throughout. Bisect remains usable. Cognitive load is bounded per session.
*Cons:* Total wall-clock is longest. No parallel work. UX wins (Phase 4) feel far away.

**Option B — Risk-bundled "big bang" PR**
Bundle Phase 0 (CI fix) + Phase 5 (dep upgrade) + Phase 3.2 (router) into one large foundation PR, then iterate on UX. ~3–4 weeks but with a single heavy review burden.
*Pros:* Foundation work clears in one go. UX phases proceed on a clean substrate.
*Cons:* Big-bang PR is hard to review, risky to revert, and conflicts with Principle 3. Single failure mode could leave the repo in a worse state than now.

**Option C — Surgical "fix blockers only, then stop"**
Only fix the 2 true Blockers (T2/T3, U5) and the drawing-save lie (F2). ~3 days. Defer everything else.
*Pros:* Minimum effort to make the product honest. Zero risk of scope creep.
*Cons:* Leaves 23 Major findings on the table indefinitely. Identity question never gets answered. Future contributors still see a contradictory codebase. Doesn't honor "plan carefully" — too minimal.

### Why Option A
- It is the only option that survives Principle 3 (one large refactor at a time). B violates it; C avoids the question by deferring all refactors.
- It is paceable: a one-developer evening-and-weekend cadence can deliver one PR every 2–4 days at the proposed phase granularity.
- It is reversible at every step: if life intervenes mid-Phase 3, the work to date is shipped and CI is still green.
- Option C's "just fix blockers" remains an emergency-exit: if scope must collapse, do Phase 0 + 2 only and stop.

### Alternatives Invalidated (for the record)
- **Rewrite from scratch:** Considered and rejected. The 13 games + canvas infra represent real working code; rewriting forfeits sunk effort and replays known bugs.
- **Hand the repo off to AI agents end-to-end (e.g. `ralph improve everything`):** Rejected. The shadow inventory of 10+ stale `claude/*` branches is precisely the failure mode this would re-trigger. Human-paced, human-merged PRs are the antidote.

---

## Pre-Execution Identity Gate

> **The owner must resolve the identity decision before Phase 1.**

The Drawing Gallery work (1.1, 1.2) is justified under **Option B (kids' learning hub)** from the report. If owner chooses **Option A (re-focus on drawing)**, scope expands (AI stencils, Firebase, PWA become in-sprint). If **Option C (split apps)**, scope changes radically.

**Default assumption:** Option B. Execution proceeds under B unless owner says otherwise.

---

## Execution Plan

### Phase 0 — Make CI honest (PR-0, ~1 day)
**Goal:** `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run type-check`, `npm run build` all green on a fresh `main` clone.

**Tasks:**
- 0.1 Add localStorage polyfill to `src/test/setup.ts`. Inline 12-line stub preferred over `jest-localstorage-mock` (which adds a dep that mismatches Vitest). Verify ShapeSorting (11) + ColorBlocks (3) tests go green.
- 0.2 Create `vitest.mobile.config.ts` (mirror `vitest.games.config.ts` with a mobile-flagged test pattern). Even if empty matchers, the script must exit 0. Add ONE smoke test under `src/test/touch.smoke.test.ts` so `test:touch` proves something.
- 0.3 `.gitignore` add: `test-results/`, `dist/`. Then `git rm -r --cached test-results dist`. Keep `svg/` decision for Phase 7 (may be referenced by stencil work).
- 0.4 Extend `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: chain `lint` → `type-check` → `test -- --run` → `test:games` → `test:touch` → `build`. Defer Lighthouse and e2e to a separate workflow on a schedule (cron) to avoid PR-blocking flake.
- 0.5 Add `webServer` stanza to `playwright.config.ts` (start vite preview on port 5173, `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`). One smoke e2e: load home page, click Sudoku, assert grid renders.

**Acceptance:**
- All 5 npm scripts exit 0 locally and in CI.
- A new PR with no source changes runs ≥4 distinct CI jobs and turns green.
- `git status` clean on `main` after un-tracking; build still works.

**Risk:** Un-tracking `dist/` could surprise GitHub Pages deploy if it serves from `dist/` on `main`. **Mitigation:** verify `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` builds from source, not from a committed `dist/`.

**Verification command:** `npm ci && npm run lint && npm run type-check && npm test -- --run && npm run test:games && npm run test:touch && npm run build` — must exit 0.

---

### Phase 1 — Restore identity credibility (PR-1a, PR-1b, ~3–5 days)
**Goal:** Drawing save loop works end-to-end; gallery is reachable; mobile clear works; daily prompt seeded.

**PR-1a (drawing save + mobile clear, ~1 day):**
- 1.1 Replace `handleDrawingChange` stub in `DrawingPage.tsx:16-19`. Implement `useDrawings()` hook returning `{drawings, save, delete, clear}` backed by localStorage key `kda:drawings:v1` (versioned per Principle from Phase 3.4 — adopt the key prefix early). Schema = `SavedDrawing[]` from SPECIFICATIONS.MD. Max 50, evict oldest by `createdAt`. Generate thumbnail via `<canvas>` toDataURL at 200×150.
- 1.3 Fix `DrawingCanvasWithTools.tsx:95` no-op. Wire `onClearCanvas` to the same `clearCanvas` ref used by the header button.

**PR-1b (gallery + daily prompt, ~2–3 days):**
- 1.2 New `src/components/Gallery/DrawingGallery.tsx`. Routes from a new home tile. Thumbnail grid 2-col mobile / 3-col tablet+. Tap thumbnail → confirm "Edit this drawing?" → loads dataURL into canvas. Delete with hold-to-confirm (kid-safe gesture). Footer: "5/50 drawings saved" pill.
- 1.4 Daily Drawing Prompt: extend `useDrawingChallenge` to read `kda:daily:lastDate` and `kda:daily:streak`. Show a "🌟 Today's Challenge" banner above the prompt list. Streak counter visible at top of Drawing Challenge home tile.

**Decision deferred:** 1.5 (DotPath PR fate) — outside this plan's scope. **Recommend** closing it for now (the PR adds work without addressing any audit finding) and re-evaluating after Phase 4 if game-variety is still a priority. Document this in `IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md` during Phase 7.

**Acceptance:**
- Draw → return to home → re-enter Drawing → previous drawing thumbnail visible in gallery.
- "Save Your Art!" footer text now matches behavior.
- Mobile tool-panel Clear button clears the canvas.
- Daily prompt updates after midnight; streak increments correctly.
- Quota-exceeded path tested manually (Safari private mode): graceful "Memory full, delete some drawings?" message, not silent failure.

**Risk:** localStorage quota (~5MB) fills after ~20–30 medium-size dataURLs. **Mitigation:** thumbnails stored separately from full dataURLs; full dataURL evicted to a "compressed" form (JPEG @ 0.7 quality) once gallery exceeds 30 entries.

---

### Phase 2 — Fix the two real Blockers (PR-2, ~1 day)
**Goal:** JellyVolleyball playable on phones; BubblePop unmount clean.

**Tasks:**
- 2.1 JellyVolleyball touch fix. In `useJellyVolleyball.ts:312-335`, multiply `e.touches[0].clientX/Y` by the inverse of `canvas.getBoundingClientRect().width / canvas.width`. Cache the ratio in a ref so it's not recomputed per move event. Also: drop the hardcoded 800×400 to viewport-relative (`min(viewport, 800) × ar`) — this also discharges finding U6 / Q5-adjacent item 4.17 for this game specifically.
- 2.2 BubblePop style cleanup. `useEffect` that injects `<style id="bubble-pop-animations">` must return a cleanup that removes the node. Alternatively, dedupe on insertion: check `document.getElementById('bubble-pop-animations')` first. Latter preferred — animations are static.

**Acceptance:**
- On a 360 CSS-px-wide viewport (Chrome DevTools), tap on left/right walls of JellyVolleyball court correctly registers as a paddle-edge tap (not an off-court miss).
- After unmounting BubblePop 5× via dev menu, `document.head.querySelectorAll('#bubble-pop-animations').length === 1`.

**Risk:** Touch-coord fix could over-correct if canvas already does its own DPR scaling. **Mitigation:** unit test with mocked `getBoundingClientRect`; manual verify on a real iOS device before merge if possible.

---

### Phase 3a — Small architecture wins (PR-3a, ~2 days)
> Note: split from full Phase 3 because 3.2 (router) is large enough to warrant its own PR.

**Tasks:**
- 3.3 Extract `getStatusColor()` from Snake/MemoryMatch into `gameUtils.ts`. Migrate both call sites.
- 3.4 Adopt `kda:` prefix on all localStorage keys. Migrate existing keys with a one-time read-old-write-new shim in a new `migrateStorage()` function called from `App.tsx` on mount. Add `kda:storage:version = "1"` sentinel; future migrations key off this. **This must run before Phase 1 ships** if Phase 1 already wrote `kda:drawings:v1` — re-sequence: do 3.4 inside PR-1a as a prerequisite.
- 3.5 Wire `playSound()` into the 4–5 games that have a "click/correct/wrong" moment but no audio: SimonSays (already has Web Audio — keep as-is), Memory Match (match found / mismatch), PopBalloons (pop), ColorBlocks (line clear), MathFacts (correct answer). Respect a `kda:settings:soundEnabled` flag (default true; mute toggle in header).
- 3.6 `usePopBalloons`: collapse 11 useState → one useReducer. Define `BalloonAction = {type: 'pop' | 'tick' | 'spawn' | 'reset' | 'combo', ...}`. Test the reducer in isolation (`src/hooks/usePopBalloons.reducer.test.ts`).
- 3.7 `useBubblePop` rAF fix. Merge the two `setGameState` calls into one functional update that both spawns and moves. Remove `gameState.bubbles.length` from the `useEffect` dep array — use a ref for the latest bubbles instead. Re-bench locally: rAF callback count per second should be ~60, not ~120.
- 3.8 Track all `setTimeout` IDs in refs and clear in `useEffect` cleanup. Touch only `useSimonSays.showSequence` and `useBubblePop.popBubble` per audit.

**Acceptance:**
- All Phase 3a changes ship with unit tests for non-trivial logic (3.6 reducer minimum).
- `getStatusColor` has exactly one definition (grep).
- All localStorage reads in code use `kda:` prefix (grep).

**Risk:** localStorage migration (3.4) could lose data if shim runs twice. **Mitigation:** sentinel-gated, with explicit "if version === '1' don't re-migrate" guard.

---

### Phase 5 — Dependency hygiene (PR-5, ~1–2 days)
> Re-sequenced before Phase 3b and Phase 4. Rationale: a11y tooling and React Router both like newer dep substrates; doing deps first means less rework.

**Tasks:**
- 5.1 Vite 5 → 6. Read Vite 6 migration notes; common gotchas: ESM-only plugin config, `define` macros, `optimizeDeps.exclude` syntax. Update `vite.config.ts`. Do NOT jump to 7/8 in this PR.
- 5.3 Vitest 1 → 3 (Vitest 4 is too new — adopt 3 LTS). Update vitest.config.ts, vitest.games.config.ts. Re-run Phase 0's polyfill setup — Vitest 3 may have shifted setup-file semantics. Compatible with Vite 6.
- 5.2 `npm audit fix` after 5.1/5.3 land (most CVEs are transitive). Re-audit; surviving HIGH vulns documented.
- 5.4 `npx update-browserslist-db@latest`.
- 5.5 Remove 3 production `console.log`s.

**Acceptance:**
- All CI jobs from Phase 0 still green on the upgraded substrate.
- `npm audit --omit=dev` shows 0 vulnerabilities (production deps).
- `npm audit` shows ≤5 dev-only vulnerabilities (no HIGH).
- `npm run dev` no longer prints the esbuild cross-origin warning.

**Risk:** Vite 6 plugin compatibility (esp. `@vitejs/plugin-react`). **Mitigation:** dry-run on a worktree before opening PR; pin to Vite 6.0.x patch if 6.1+ has breaking plugin changes; rollback strategy = single PR revert.

---

### Phase 3b — Router migration (PR-3b, ~3 days)
> Split out due to blast radius. This PR touches App.tsx + HomePage.tsx + every game's "return to home" button.

**Tasks:**
- 3.2 Adopt `react-router-dom@6`. `App.tsx` becomes a `<RouterProvider>`. Routes: `/`, `/games/:gameId`, `/drawing`, `/drawing/gallery`. `HomePage` becomes a leaf component — drop the 14 nav callback props. Each game's "Home" button becomes `<Link to="/">` or `navigate(-1)`.
- Restructure data: `GAMES_REGISTRY` const in `src/components/Games/registry.ts` mapping `id → {label, icon, ageBadge, Component}`. `HomePage` reads it; routing reads it; new games drop in by adding one entry.

**Acceptance:**
- Browser back button works between Home and any game.
- Deep-link `/games/sudoku` opens Sudoku directly.
- `HomePage.tsx` props down to ≤2.
- All 13 games still navigate correctly home (manual checklist + 1 e2e click-each-tile test).
- DotPath PR (if still open) merges cleanly because of registry pattern.

**Risk:** This is the **highest blast-radius PR in the plan**. **Mitigations:**
- Land Phase 3a (game-shell consolidation prereq already shipped) before this.
- Add an e2e test that clicks every home tile and verifies the URL changes — guards against silent breakage.
- Land with a feature flag: `import.meta.env.VITE_USE_ROUTER` defaulting to true; if production blows up, set false in `.env.production` and revert immediately. Remove flag in next PR.

---

### Phase 3.1 — Standardize on GameLayout (PR-3c, ~2 days)
> Done AFTER router migration so the GameLayout's Home button uses `useNavigate` not a callback prop.

- 3.1 Migrate ColorBlocksGame, JellyVolleyball, Snake, Sudoku, Tetris to `<GameLayout>`. Each is ~30 LOC of inline header swapped for ~5 LOC GameLayout invocation. Visual diff per game documented in PR description with before/after screenshots.

**Acceptance:**
- `grep -L 'GameLayout' src/components/Games/*/[A-Z]*Page.tsx` returns empty (every game uses it).
- Visual regression: no game looks worse than before; ideally all look more consistent.

**Risk:** Visual regressions on the 5 migrated games. **Mitigation:** screenshot diff against `main` for each; reviewer (or kid) checks before merge.

---

### Phase 4 — UX & accessibility (PR-4a through PR-4e, ~2 weeks)
> Split into 5 themed PRs for review tractability. Order chosen so kid-facing wins land before screen-reader wins.

**PR-4a — Kid-facing polish (~3 days):**
- 4.6 Pictographic difficulty selectors (replace text "Easy/Medium/Hard" with 🐣/🐱/🦁 buttons across 7 games)
- 4.13 Drawing Undo/Redo (canvas history stack, max 20 frames)
- 4.13 Sudoku hint (highlight a single correct cell on demand, max 3 hints/game)
- 4.12 Celebratory win modals (confetti via `canvas-confetti`, sound effect from playSound)
- 4.14 First-run onboarding overlay: pictographic 4-step tour, dismissible, gated on `kda:firstRunComplete`

**PR-4b — Accessibility compliance (~3 days):**
- 4.1 aria-label every home tile
- 4.3 Restore focus-visible globally (`*:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--ring) }`)
- 4.4 Simon Says: add patterns or position labels to colored buttons (e.g. icons inside each button)
- 4.10 ColorPicker keyboard activation (`onKeyDown`)
- 4.11 MathFacts input `<label>`
- 4.5 `document.title` updates on route change (now feasible thanks to PR-3b router)

**PR-4c — Motion & focus (~1 day):**
- 4.2 `prefers-reduced-motion` media query gating animations
- 4.15 `visibilitychange` pause for JellyVolleyball, Snake, PopBalloons
- 4.16 Font preconnect + `font-display: swap` (move `@import` to `<link>`)
- 4.18 Constrain `touch-action: manipulation` to game canvases, not `*`
- 4.19 React.memo TetrisBoard cells

**PR-4d — Mobile layout (~2 days):**
- 4.7 Age badge on each home tile (Stage 6's age table → tiny pill on each card)
- 4.8 Mobile "How to play" affordance (collapsible ⓘ button per game)
- 4.9 Differentiate the 3 🎨-emoji tiles (use 🟪 / 🖌️ / 🌈 instead)
- 4.17 Viewport-relative game canvases (BubblePop, JellyVolleyball already done in Phase 2)

**PR-4e — Stretch polish (optional, ~1 day):**
- 4.19 if not done above
- Any leftovers

**Acceptance:**
- Lighthouse mobile a11y score ≥ 90 (this becomes measurable now that `lighthouserc-mobile.js` is written in Phase 4c).
- Reduced-motion: all `animate-*` animations cease when OS setting is on.
- Keyboard-only navigation can reach and activate every home tile and every game's primary controls.

**Risk:** PR-4a includes a new dep (`canvas-confetti`, ~5KB). **Mitigation:** evaluate if a hand-rolled CSS-particles animation works (free) before adding the dep.

---

## Out of scope (this plan)

The following are **explicitly deferred** to a follow-up roadmap document. They are not bad ideas — they're just not the resurrection sprint.

| Deferred item | Why | When to revisit |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 6 variety menu (Sound Painter, Tracing, Letter Tracing, Color-by-Number, Storybook, Parent Dashboard, etc.) | Feature work; resurrection is consolidation | After Phase 4 lands and the owner re-engages |
| Phase 7 repo hygiene (archive plan docs, branch triage, code-split, flood-fill perf) | Polish; not blocking | Slot one item per sprint as background work |
| Arcade-branch triage (6 games + 1 WIP) | Separate sub-project; needs per-game quality review | Standalone audit, post-resurrection |
| PWA / Service Worker / Firebase / AI Stencils | Requires identity Option A commitment | After identity gate resolves to A |
| React 18 → 19, Vite 6 → 8, Vitest 3 → 4, Tailwind 3 → 4 | Major-version chains beyond minimum-viable upgrade | Once Phase 5 lands, slot as periodic maintenance |
| Code-split per-game bundles (Q7) | Bundle is 49KB gzip; below any practical threshold | When bundle crosses 200KB gzip |
| Flood-fill Uint8Array bitset (Q5) | Performance optimization with no observed jank | If/when a kid actually reports it |

---

## Verification plan (per PR and overall)

**Per-PR gates (all PRs):**
1. `npm run lint && npm run type-check && npm test -- --run && npm run build` exit 0
2. CI workflow turns green
3. Manual smoke on a real iOS Safari or Chrome DevTools device emulation (especially touch-handling PRs)
4. PR description includes: which findings it closes, screenshots before/after if visual, rollback steps if non-trivial

**End-of-sprint verification:**
- All 2 Blockers closed
- ≥20 of 23 Majors closed (>85%)
- Lighthouse mobile a11y ≥ 90, perf ≥ 80
- A 5-minute user-test session with the actual primary user (the dev's daughter) — observe pain points
- `IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md` rewritten to reflect post-resurrection state

---

## ADR Summary

**Decision:** Resurrect the project via Option A (sequential phased sprint), under identity Option B (kids' learning hub), with router migration deferred until after dep upgrades.

**Drivers:** time-to-honest-product; safe pace for a single dev; unresolved identity ambiguity.

**Alternatives considered:** big-bang PR (rejected: violates small-PR principle), blockers-only (rejected: leaves 23 majors untouched), full rewrite (rejected: forfeits working code).

**Consequences:** ~6 weeks of evening/weekend work; predictable per-PR review burden; reversible at every step. Owner must resolve identity gate before Phase 1.

**Follow-ups:** Phase 6 variety menu; arcade-branch triage; PWA/Firebase if Option A re-chosen later; major-version dep chases (React 19, Vitest 4).

---

**Status:** Draft v1 — awaiting Architect (Gemini) review.

## RALPLAN-DR Summary

### Principles (in priority order)
1. **Restore trust before adding features.** Green CI and an honest drawing-save loop come before anything new. The product currently lies to the user ("automatically saved!" while doing nothing) and to its CI ("tests pass" while 14 fail). Trust is the precondition for every other improvement.
2. **Small, reversible PRs.** Resurrection means re-engaging cognitive load on a stale repo. Every PR should be reviewable in <30 min and revertable in <5 min. No multi-week branches.
3. **One blast-radius-large refactor at a time.** Router migration, dep upgrades, and game-shell standardization each touch many files. They cannot land in the same week without thrashing review and breaking bisect.
4. **Defer scope, don't expand it.** The audit produced ~50 findings and a 10-game variety menu. The resurrection sprint commits to the first 4 phases (~30 items). Everything else (Phase 6 features, Phase 7 hygiene, the arcade-branch triage) becomes a roadmap document, not a sprint task.
5. **Honor the primary user.** The dev's daughter — likely ages 4–8 — is the only real user. Optimize for her: large touch targets, mobile-first, no-text difficulty, undo/restart prominence. Accessibility for screen readers etc. is also worth doing, but the priority is the kid playing on the phone.

### Decision Drivers (top 3)
1. **Time-to-honest-product.** How fast can the user re-engage the repo with confidence that what's shipped matches what's promised? Drives the placement of Phases 0–1 first.
2. **Safe rate of change.** This is a one-developer project that's been dormant. The plan must be paceable by one human, with reverts trivially possible. Drives small-PR principle and the dep-upgrade quarantine.
3. **Identity ambiguity unresolved.** Whether to commit to drawing-app, games-hub, or hybrid is a strategic decision the planner cannot make. Drives the **Identity Gate** at the very top of execution.

### Viable Options

**Option A — Sequential phased sprint (this plan's recommendation)**
Run Phases 0 → 1 → 2 → 3a (small) → 5 → 3b (router) → 4 in order, each phase landing as a small PR (or PR series) with green CI before the next phase opens. ~6 weeks at a comfortable pace for one developer.
*Pros:* Each PR is small and revertable. CI stays green throughout. Bisect remains usable. Cognitive load is bounded per session.
*Cons:* Total wall-clock is longest. No parallel work. UX wins (Phase 4) feel far away.

**Option B — Risk-bundled "big bang" PR**
Bundle Phase 0 (CI fix) + Phase 5 (dep upgrade) + Phase 3.2 (router) into one large foundation PR, then iterate on UX. ~3–4 weeks but with a single heavy review burden.
*Pros:* Foundation work clears in one go. UX phases proceed on a clean substrate.
*Cons:* Big-bang PR is hard to review, risky to revert, and conflicts with Principle 3. Single failure mode could leave the repo in a worse state than now.

**Option C — Surgical "fix blockers only, then stop"**
Only fix the 2 true Blockers (T2/T3, U5) and the drawing-save lie (F2). ~3 days. Defer everything else.
*Pros:* Minimum effort to make the product honest. Zero risk of scope creep.
*Cons:* Leaves 23 Major findings on the table indefinitely. Identity question never gets answered. Future contributors still see a contradictory codebase. Doesn't honor "plan carefully" — too minimal.

### Why Option A
- It is the only option that survives Principle 3 (one large refactor at a time). B violates it; C avoids the question by deferring all refactors.
- It is paceable: a one-developer evening-and-weekend cadence can deliver one PR every 2–4 days at the proposed phase granularity.
- It is reversible at every step: if life intervenes mid-Phase 3, the work to date is shipped and CI is still green.
- Option C's "just fix blockers" remains an emergency-exit: if scope must collapse, do Phase 0 + 2 only and stop.

### Alternatives Invalidated (for the record)
- **Rewrite from scratch:** Considered and rejected. The 13 games + canvas infra represent real working code; rewriting forfeits sunk effort and replays known bugs.
- **Hand the repo off to AI agents end-to-end (e.g. `ralph improve everything`):** Rejected. The shadow inventory of 10+ stale `claude/*` branches is precisely the failure mode this would re-trigger. Human-paced, human-merged PRs are the antidote.

---

## Pre-Execution Identity Gate

> **The owner must resolve the identity decision before Phase 1.**

The Drawing Gallery work (1.1, 1.2) is justified under **Option B (kids' learning hub)** from the report. If owner chooses **Option A (re-focus on drawing)**, scope expands (AI stencils, Firebase, PWA become in-sprint). If **Option C (split apps)**, scope changes radically.

**Default assumption:** Option B. Execution proceeds under B unless owner says otherwise.

---

## Execution Plan

### Phase 0 — Make CI honest (PR-0, ~1 day)
**Goal:** `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run type-check`, `npm run build` all green on a fresh `main` clone.

**Tasks:**
- 0.1 Add localStorage polyfill to `src/test/setup.ts`. Inline 12-line stub preferred over `jest-localstorage-mock` (which adds a dep that mismatches Vitest). Verify ShapeSorting (11) + ColorBlocks (3) tests go green.
- 0.2 Create `vitest.mobile.config.ts` (mirror `vitest.games.config.ts` with a mobile-flagged test pattern). Even if empty matchers, the script must exit 0. Add ONE smoke test under `src/test/touch.smoke.test.ts` so `test:touch` proves something.
- 0.3 `.gitignore` add: `test-results/`, `dist/`. Then `git rm -r --cached test-results dist`. Keep `svg/` decision for Phase 7 (may be referenced by stencil work).
- 0.4 Extend `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: chain `lint` → `type-check` → `test -- --run` → `test:games` → `test:touch` → `build`. Defer Lighthouse and e2e to a separate workflow on a schedule (cron) to avoid PR-blocking flake.
- 0.5 Add `webServer` stanza to `playwright.config.ts` (start vite preview on port 5173, `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`). One smoke e2e: load home page, click Sudoku, assert grid renders.

**Acceptance:**
- All 5 npm scripts exit 0 locally and in CI.
- A new PR with no source changes runs ≥4 distinct CI jobs and turns green.
- `git status` clean on `main` after un-tracking; build still works.

**Risk:** Un-tracking `dist/` could surprise GitHub Pages deploy if it serves from `dist/` on `main`. **Mitigation:** verify `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` builds from source, not from a committed `dist/`.

**Verification command:** `npm ci && npm run lint && npm run type-check && npm test -- --run && npm run test:games && npm run test:touch && npm run build` — must exit 0.

---

### Phase 1 — Restore identity credibility (PR-1a, PR-1b, ~3–5 days)
**Goal:** Drawing save loop works end-to-end; gallery is reachable; mobile clear works; daily prompt seeded.

**PR-1a (drawing save + mobile clear, ~1 day):**
- 1.1 Replace `handleDrawingChange` stub in `DrawingPage.tsx:16-19`. Implement `useDrawings()` hook returning `{drawings, save, delete, clear}` backed by localStorage key `kda:drawings:v1` (versioned per Principle from Phase 3.4 — adopt the key prefix early). Schema = `SavedDrawing[]` from SPECIFICATIONS.MD. Max 50, evict oldest by `createdAt`. Generate thumbnail via `<canvas>` toDataURL at 200×150.
- 1.3 Fix `DrawingCanvasWithTools.tsx:95` no-op. Wire `onClearCanvas` to the same `clearCanvas` ref used by the header button.

**PR-1b (gallery + daily prompt, ~2–3 days):**
- 1.2 New `src/components/Gallery/DrawingGallery.tsx`. Routes from a new home tile. Thumbnail grid 2-col mobile / 3-col tablet+. Tap thumbnail → confirm "Edit this drawing?" → loads dataURL into canvas. Delete with hold-to-confirm (kid-safe gesture). Footer: "5/50 drawings saved" pill.
- 1.4 Daily Drawing Prompt: extend `useDrawingChallenge` to read `kda:daily:lastDate` and `kda:daily:streak`. Show a "🌟 Today's Challenge" banner above the prompt list. Streak counter visible at top of Drawing Challenge home tile.

**Decision deferred:** 1.5 (DotPath PR fate) — outside this plan's scope. **Recommend** closing it for now (the PR adds work without addressing any audit finding) and re-evaluating after Phase 4 if game-variety is still a priority. Document this in `IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md` during Phase 7.

**Acceptance:**
- Draw → return to home → re-enter Drawing → previous drawing thumbnail visible in gallery.
- "Save Your Art!" footer text now matches behavior.
- Mobile tool-panel Clear button clears the canvas.
- Daily prompt updates after midnight; streak increments correctly.
- Quota-exceeded path tested manually (Safari private mode): graceful "Memory full, delete some drawings?" message, not silent failure.

**Risk:** localStorage quota (~5MB) fills after ~20–30 medium-size dataURLs. **Mitigation:** thumbnails stored separately from full dataURLs; full dataURL evicted to a "compressed" form (JPEG @ 0.7 quality) once gallery exceeds 30 entries.

---

### Phase 2 — Fix the two real Blockers (PR-2, ~1 day)
**Goal:** JellyVolleyball playable on phones; BubblePop unmount clean.

**Tasks:**
- 2.1 JellyVolleyball touch fix. In `useJellyVolleyball.ts:312-335`, multiply `e.touches[0].clientX/Y` by the inverse of `canvas.getBoundingClientRect().width / canvas.width`. Cache the ratio in a ref so it's not recomputed per move event. Also: drop the hardcoded 800×400 to viewport-relative (`min(viewport, 800) × ar`) — this also discharges finding U6 / Q5-adjacent item 4.17 for this game specifically.
- 2.2 BubblePop style cleanup. `useEffect` that injects `<style id="bubble-pop-animations">` must return a cleanup that removes the node. Alternatively, dedupe on insertion: check `document.getElementById('bubble-pop-animations')` first. Latter preferred — animations are static.

**Acceptance:**
- On a 360 CSS-px-wide viewport (Chrome DevTools), tap on left/right walls of JellyVolleyball court correctly registers as a paddle-edge tap (not an off-court miss).
- After unmounting BubblePop 5× via dev menu, `document.head.querySelectorAll('#bubble-pop-animations').length === 1`.

**Risk:** Touch-coord fix could over-correct if canvas already does its own DPR scaling. **Mitigation:** unit test with mocked `getBoundingClientRect`; manual verify on a real iOS device before merge if possible.

---

### Phase 3a — Small architecture wins (PR-3a, ~2 days)
> Note: split from full Phase 3 because 3.2 (router) is large enough to warrant its own PR.

**Tasks:**
- 3.3 Extract `getStatusColor()` from Snake/MemoryMatch into `gameUtils.ts`. Migrate both call sites.
- 3.4 Adopt `kda:` prefix on all localStorage keys. Migrate existing keys with a one-time read-old-write-new shim in a new `migrateStorage()` function called from `App.tsx` on mount. Add `kda:storage:version = "1"` sentinel; future migrations key off this. **This must run before Phase 1 ships** if Phase 1 already wrote `kda:drawings:v1` — re-sequence: do 3.4 inside PR-1a as a prerequisite.
- 3.5 Wire `playSound()` into the 4–5 games that have a "click/correct/wrong" moment but no audio: SimonSays (already has Web Audio — keep as-is), Memory Match (match found / mismatch), PopBalloons (pop), ColorBlocks (line clear), MathFacts (correct answer). Respect a `kda:settings:soundEnabled` flag (default true; mute toggle in header).
- 3.6 `usePopBalloons`: collapse 11 useState → one useReducer. Define `BalloonAction = {type: 'pop' | 'tick' | 'spawn' | 'reset' | 'combo', ...}`. Test the reducer in isolation (`src/hooks/usePopBalloons.reducer.test.ts`).
- 3.7 `useBubblePop` rAF fix. Merge the two `setGameState` calls into one functional update that both spawns and moves. Remove `gameState.bubbles.length` from the `useEffect` dep array — use a ref for the latest bubbles instead. Re-bench locally: rAF callback count per second should be ~60, not ~120.
- 3.8 Track all `setTimeout` IDs in refs and clear in `useEffect` cleanup. Touch only `useSimonSays.showSequence` and `useBubblePop.popBubble` per audit.

**Acceptance:**
- All Phase 3a changes ship with unit tests for non-trivial logic (3.6 reducer minimum).
- `getStatusColor` has exactly one definition (grep).
- All localStorage reads in code use `kda:` prefix (grep).

**Risk:** localStorage migration (3.4) could lose data if shim runs twice. **Mitigation:** sentinel-gated, with explicit "if version === '1' don't re-migrate" guard.

---

### Phase 5 — Dependency hygiene (PR-5, ~1–2 days)
> Re-sequenced before Phase 3b and Phase 4. Rationale: a11y tooling and React Router both like newer dep substrates; doing deps first means less rework.

**Tasks:**
- 5.1 Vite 5 → 6. Read Vite 6 migration notes; common gotchas: ESM-only plugin config, `define` macros, `optimizeDeps.exclude` syntax. Update `vite.config.ts`. Do NOT jump to 7/8 in this PR.
- 5.3 Vitest 1 → 3 (Vitest 4 is too new — adopt 3 LTS). Update vitest.config.ts, vitest.games.config.ts. Re-run Phase 0's polyfill setup — Vitest 3 may have shifted setup-file semantics. Compatible with Vite 6.
- 5.2 `npm audit fix` after 5.1/5.3 land (most CVEs are transitive). Re-audit; surviving HIGH vulns documented.
- 5.4 `npx update-browserslist-db@latest`.
- 5.5 Remove 3 production `console.log`s.

**Acceptance:**
- All CI jobs from Phase 0 still green on the upgraded substrate.
- `npm audit --omit=dev` shows 0 vulnerabilities (production deps).
- `npm audit` shows ≤5 dev-only vulnerabilities (no HIGH).
- `npm run dev` no longer prints the esbuild cross-origin warning.

**Risk:** Vite 6 plugin compatibility (esp. `@vitejs/plugin-react`). **Mitigation:** dry-run on a worktree before opening PR; pin to Vite 6.0.x patch if 6.1+ has breaking plugin changes; rollback strategy = single PR revert.

---

### Phase 3b — Router migration (PR-3b, ~3 days)
> Split out due to blast radius. This PR touches App.tsx + HomePage.tsx + every game's "return to home" button.

**Tasks:**
- 3.2 Adopt `react-router-dom@6`. `App.tsx` becomes a `<RouterProvider>`. Routes: `/`, `/games/:gameId`, `/drawing`, `/drawing/gallery`. `HomePage` becomes a leaf component — drop the 14 nav callback props. Each game's "Home" button becomes `<Link to="/">` or `navigate(-1)`.
- Restructure data: `GAMES_REGISTRY` const in `src/components/Games/registry.ts` mapping `id → {label, icon, ageBadge, Component}`. `HomePage` reads it; routing reads it; new games drop in by adding one entry.

**Acceptance:**
- Browser back button works between Home and any game.
- Deep-link `/games/sudoku` opens Sudoku directly.
- `HomePage.tsx` props down to ≤2.
- All 13 games still navigate correctly home (manual checklist + 1 e2e click-each-tile test).
- DotPath PR (if still open) merges cleanly because of registry pattern.

**Risk:** This is the **highest blast-radius PR in the plan**. **Mitigations:**
- Land Phase 3a (game-shell consolidation prereq already shipped) before this.
- Add an e2e test that clicks every home tile and verifies the URL changes — guards against silent breakage.
- Land with a feature flag: `import.meta.env.VITE_USE_ROUTER` defaulting to true; if production blows up, set false in `.env.production` and revert immediately. Remove flag in next PR.

---

### Phase 3.1 — Standardize on GameLayout (PR-3c, ~2 days)
> Done AFTER router migration so the GameLayout's Home button uses `useNavigate` not a callback prop.

- 3.1 Migrate ColorBlocksGame, JellyVolleyball, Snake, Sudoku, Tetris to `<GameLayout>`. Each is ~30 LOC of inline header swapped for ~5 LOC GameLayout invocation. Visual diff per game documented in PR description with before/after screenshots.

**Acceptance:**
- `grep -L 'GameLayout' src/components/Games/*/[A-Z]*Page.tsx` returns empty (every game uses it).
- Visual regression: no game looks worse than before; ideally all look more consistent.

**Risk:** Visual regressions on the 5 migrated games. **Mitigation:** screenshot diff against `main` for each; reviewer (or kid) checks before merge.

---

### Phase 4 — UX & accessibility (PR-4a through PR-4e, ~2 weeks)
> Split into 5 themed PRs for review tractability. Order chosen so kid-facing wins land before screen-reader wins.

**PR-4a — Kid-facing polish (~3 days):**
- 4.6 Pictographic difficulty selectors (replace text "Easy/Medium/Hard" with 🐣/🐱/🦁 buttons across 7 games)
- 4.13 Drawing Undo/Redo (canvas history stack, max 20 frames)
- 4.13 Sudoku hint (highlight a single correct cell on demand, max 3 hints/game)
- 4.12 Celebratory win modals (confetti via `canvas-confetti`, sound effect from playSound)
- 4.14 First-run onboarding overlay: pictographic 4-step tour, dismissible, gated on `kda:firstRunComplete`

**PR-4b — Accessibility compliance (~3 days):**
- 4.1 aria-label every home tile
- 4.3 Restore focus-visible globally (`*:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--ring) }`)
- 4.4 Simon Says: add patterns or position labels to colored buttons (e.g. icons inside each button)
- 4.10 ColorPicker keyboard activation (`onKeyDown`)
- 4.11 MathFacts input `<label>`
- 4.5 `document.title` updates on route change (now feasible thanks to PR-3b router)

**PR-4c — Motion & focus (~1 day):**
- 4.2 `prefers-reduced-motion` media query gating animations
- 4.15 `visibilitychange` pause for JellyVolleyball, Snake, PopBalloons
- 4.16 Font preconnect + `font-display: swap` (move `@import` to `<link>`)
- 4.18 Constrain `touch-action: manipulation` to game canvases, not `*`
- 4.19 React.memo TetrisBoard cells

**PR-4d — Mobile layout (~2 days):**
- 4.7 Age badge on each home tile (Stage 6's age table → tiny pill on each card)
- 4.8 Mobile "How to play" affordance (collapsible ⓘ button per game)

- 4.19 if not done above
- Any leftovers

**Acceptance:**
- Lighthouse mobile a11y score ≥ 90 (this becomes measurable now that `lighthouserc-mobile.js` is written in Phase 4c).
- Reduced-motion: all `animate-*` animations cease when OS setting is on.
- Keyboard-only navigation can reach and activate every home tile and every game's primary controls.

**Risk:** PR-4a includes a new dep (`canvas-confetti`, ~5KB). **Mitigation:** evaluate if a hand-rolled CSS-particles animation works (free) before adding the dep.

## Out of scope (this plan)

The following are **explicitly deferred** to a follow-up roadmap document. They are not bad ideas — they're just not the resurrection sprint.

| Deferred item | Why | When to revisit |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 6 variety menu (Sound Painter, Tracing, Letter Tracing, Color-by-Number, Storybook, Parent Dashboard, etc.) | Feature work; resurrection is consolidation | After Phase 4 lands and the owner re-engages |
| Phase 7 repo hygiene (archive plan docs, branch triage, code-split, flood-fill perf) | Polish; not blocking | Slot one item per sprint as background work |
| Arcade-branch triage (6 games + 1 WIP) | Separate sub-project; needs per-game quality review | Standalone audit, post-resurrection |
| PWA / Service Worker / Firebase / AI Stencils | Requires identity Option A commitment | After identity gate resolves to A |
| React 18 → 19, Vite 6 → 8, Vitest 3 → 4, Tailwind 3 → 4 | Major-version chains beyond minimum-viable upgrade | Once Phase 5 lands, slot as periodic maintenance |
| Code-split per-game bundles (Q7) | Bundle is 49KB gzip; below any practical threshold | When bundle crosses 200KB gzip |
| Flood-fill Uint8Array bitset (Q5) | Performance optimization with no observed jank | If/when a kid actually reports it |

---

## Verification plan (per PR and overall)

**Per-PR gates (all PRs):**
1. `npm run lint && npm run type-check && npm test -- --run && npm run build` exit 0
2. CI workflow turns green
3. Manual smoke on a real iOS Safari or Chrome DevTools device emulation (especially touch-handling PRs)
4. PR description includes: which findings it closes, screenshots before/after if visual, rollback steps if non-trivial

**End-of-sprint verification:**
- All 2 Blockers closed
- ≥20 of 23 Majors closed (>85%)
- Lighthouse mobile a11y ≥ 90, perf ≥ 80
- A 5-minute user-test session with the actual primary user (the dev's daughter) — observe pain points
- `IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md` rewritten to reflect post-resurrection state

---

## ADR Summary

**Decision:** Resurrect the project via Option A (sequential phased sprint), under identity Option B (kids' learning hub), with router migration deferred until after dep upgrades.

**Drivers:** time-to-honest-product; safe pace for a single dev; unresolved identity ambiguity.

**Alternatives considered:** big-bang PR (rejected: violates small-PR principle), blockers-only (rejected: leaves 23 majors untouched), full rewrite (rejected: forfeits working code).

**Consequences:** ~6 weeks of evening/weekend work; predictable per-PR review burden; reversible at every step. Owner must resolve identity gate before Phase 1.

**Follow-ups:** Phase 6 variety menu; arcade-branch triage; PWA/Firebase if Option A re-chosen later; major-version dep chases (React 19, Vitest 4).

---

agy -p "$(cat <<'PROMPT'
You are acting as ARCHITECT in a consensus planning loop for a software resurrection project. Your job is NOT to rubber-stamp. Provide the strongest steelman antithesis, surface at least one real tradeoff tension the planner did not adequately address, and propose a synthesis where possible. Flag any principle violations.

CONTEXT FILES (read these from the workspace):
- /Users/yp/work/kids-drawing-app/.omc/research/resurrect-20260521/report.md  (the audit findings being addressed)
- /Users/yp/work/kids-drawing-app/.omc/plans/resurrect-20260521-plan-v1.md  (the plan you are reviewing)
- /Users/yp/work/kids-drawing-app/.omc/research/resurrect-20260521/verification.md  (cross-validation corrections)

PROJECT BACKGROUND:
- Single-developer hobby project. User is rebuilding for his ~4-8yo daughter.
- Started as 'kids drawing app', drifted to mini-games hub (13 games on main).
- 6-week resurrection sprint window roughly.
- The audit produced ~50 findings (2 Blockers, 23 Majors, ~30 Minors).
- Plan organizes work into Phases 0-4 + Phase 5 (deps) + deferred Phases 6-7.

YOUR REVIEW FRAMEWORK:
1) SEQUENCING - Is the phase order defensible? Are there hidden dependencies between phases the planner missed? Could a phase be moved earlier/later for less risk or higher ROI?
2) BLAST RADIUS - The plan promises 'small reversible PRs.' Are any phases actually too large to land safely as proposed? Are any too granular to be efficient?
3) STEELMAN ANTITHESIS - Make the strongest possible case for an option the planner rejected (B 'big bang' or C 'blockers only'). What would a reasonable architect prefer that path?
4) HIDDEN COST - The plan claims ~6 weeks for a single dev at evening/weekend pace. Is that realistic given the scope? What's missing from the timeline?
5) PRINCIPLE VIOLATIONS - The plan's 5 principles: restore trust before features; small reversible PRs; one large refactor at a time; defer don't expand; honor the primary user. Does any task in the plan violate one of these principles?
6) TEST/VERIFY GAPS - Are the per-phase acceptance criteria actually testable? Is anything declared 'done' that has no objective measure?
7) RISK ITEMS UNDER-ADDRESSED - The plan calls out risks but are mitigations concrete? Anything that handwaves a risk?
8) THE ONE THING - If you could change ONE thing about this plan to make it materially better, what would it be?

[Bullet list with phase numbers and reasoning.]

### Blast-radius concerns
[Which phases are too large/small to land safely as PRs. Specific.]

### Test/verify gaps
[Which acceptance criteria are unmeasurable or hand-wavy.]

### The one thing
[The single highest-leverage change to the plan, in 2-3 sentences.]

### Verdict
One of:
- READY_FOR_CRITIC (the plan is sound; revisions are nice-to-have)
- REVISE_THEN_RECHECK (the plan needs material revisions before Critic should see it)
- REJECT (fundamental problems; suggest restart)

Be candid. The planner is a peer, not a junior; sycophantic praise wastes the loop. Flag the real issues.

136	## Architect Review — Plan v1
137	
138	### Steelman antithesis
139	The planner summarily rejected Option C ("fix blockers only, then stop") as "too minimal" and leaving the "identity question never answered." However, for a single-developer evening/weekend hobby project, Option C is objectively the safest and most realistic path. The "identity crisis" is a developer-centric architectural concern, not a user-centric one—a 4-year-old child does not care if the URL says "kids-drawing-app" while they are happily playing BubblePop. 
140	
141	By committing to a 6-week slog of router migrations, dependency upgrades, and layout refactorings on a completely untested 13-game codebase, the plan introduces massive regression risk and burnout potential. The project has already stalled once. Option C guarantees a 100% success rate in Week 1: CI is green, the lying save button is fixed, and the broken JellyVolleyball game works. Banking this win and walking away preserves the developer's energy and leaves the codebase perfectly stable. Features and refactors can then be pulled strictly on-demand when the actual primary user asks for them.
142	
143	### Real tradeoff tension
144	The plan fails to resolve the tension between **Architecture Coherence** and the **Lack of Game Unit Tests**. The audit explicitly stated there are *zero* unit tests for the 14 games. Yet, the plan schedules a massive Router migration (Phase 3b) and GameLayout standardization (Phase 3.1) across all of them. The hidden cost here is immense manual QA overhead. You cannot safely execute sweeping architectural changes across 13 untested games in "small, reversible" weekend PRs without either introducing subtle regressions or spending 80% of your time manually tapping through every game on a phone. The plan pretends these refactors are safe because the PRs are labeled "small," but the blast radius of a root router swap in an untested hub is inherently unsafe.
145	
146	### Synthesis proposal
147	To resolve this tension, invert the sprint priority: deliver user value first, and gate the architecture work behind test coverage. Sequence the work as: CI Fixes (Phase 0) → Shipped Blockers (Phase 2) → Kid-Facing Polish (Phase 4a) → Drawing Identity (Phase 1). Move the Router migration (Phase 3b) and Vite upgrades (Phase 5) to the very end of the sprint. Before executing the Router migration, mandate the creation of a programmatic Playwright smoke test that loops through the game registry, loads every game, and clicks "Home" to automate the QA burden.
148	
149	### Principle violations
150	*   **Principle 1 (Restore trust before features):** Violated by sequencing Phase 1 (adding a new Drawing Gallery feature) *before* Phase 2 (fixing the JellyVolleyball unplayable Blocker). Shipped broken code must be fixed before writing new feature code.
151	*   **Principle 2 (Small reversible PRs):** Violated by PR-3b (Router migration). The plan suggests feature-flagging the new router. You cannot safely feature-flag React Router hooks (`useNavigate`) inside leaf game components while falling back to a `useState` router; the hooks will throw runtime errors if rendered outside a `<Router>` context. Attempting to build a safe fallback bridge for this will create a massive, tangled, unreviewable diff.
152	*   **Principle 5 (Honor the primary user):** Violated by prioritizing Vite 6 upgrades and React Router (invisible to the user) weeks ahead of Phase 4a (pictographic difficulty selectors and win modals, which directly impact a 4-year-old's ability to play and enjoy the app).
153	
154	### Sequencing concerns
155	*   **Phase 2 before Phase 1:** Blockers (JellyVolleyball touch) must be fixed before adding new features (Drawing Gallery).
156	*   **Phase 4a before Phase 3/5:** Kid-facing UX polish (Phase 4a) requires no major architectural changes and delivers immediate value to the child. It should be pulled forward to Week 2.
157	*   **Phase 3.4 (LocalStorage prefix):** Moving this into PR-1a makes PR-1a both a feature PR and a global data-migration PR. This mixes concerns. Run the storage migration as its own isolated PR *before* PR-1a.
158	*   **Phase 3.1 (GameLayout) after 3b (Router):** Standardizing the game layouts *before* swapping the router reduces the number of disparate `navigate` implementations the router PR has to hunt down and fix. 
159	
160	### Blast-radius concerns
161	*   **PR-3b (Router Migration):** Touching the root `App.tsx`, the `HomePage.tsx` monolith, and 13 individual game components in one PR is too large. This needs to be split: PR1 creates the `registry.ts` and refactors `HomePage` to use it (data-driven UI), PR2 standardizes the GameLayouts, and PR3 actually introduces `react-router-dom`.
162	*   **PR-4a (Kid-facing polish):** Bundling Undo/Redo (complex canvas state array management), Sudoku hints (complex game logic), Win modals, AND First-run onboarding into a single "~3 day" PR is wildly optimistic. Undo/Redo is notoriously edge-case heavy and warrants its own PR entirely.
163	
164	### Test/verify gaps
165	*   **Phase 1 PR-1a (Drawing save):** "Quota-exceeded path tested manually." This is highly prone to regression. It needs a Vitest unit test that mocks `localStorage.setItem` to throw a `DOMException` (QuotaExceededError) to prove the graceful degradation works.
166	*   **Phase 3b (Router):** Relying on a "manual checklist" to verify 13 games navigate home safely after a root router swap is brittle and exhausting.
167	*   **Phase 4d (Mobile layout):** Viewport-relative game sizing acceptance criteria are missing. Objective metrics (e.g., verifying canvas width does not exceed `window.innerWidth` via Playwright) are needed to prove it isn't broken on smaller screens.
168	
169	### The one thing
170	Move Phase 2 (Blockers) and Phase 4a (Kid-facing polish) immediately after Phase 0 to deliver tangible value to the 4-year-old in Week 1, and push the high-risk Router/Vite refactors to the end of the sprint where they are gated by automated Playwright smoke tests.

## Architect Review — Plan v1

### Steelman antithesis
The planner summarily rejected Option C ("fix blockers only, then stop") as "too minimal" and leaving the "identity question never answered." However, for a single-developer evening/weekend hobby project, Option C is objectively the safest and most realistic path. The "identity crisis" is a developer-centric architectural concern, not a user-centric one—a 4-year-old child does not care if the URL says "kids-drawing-app" while they are happily playing BubblePop. 

By committing to a 6-week slog of router migrations, dependency upgrades, and layout refactorings on a completely untested 13-game codebase, the plan introduces massive regression risk and burnout potential. The project has already stalled once. Option C guarantees a 100% success rate in Week 1: CI is green, the lying save button is fixed, and the broken JellyVolleyball game works. Banking this win and walking away preserves the developer's energy and leaves the codebase perfectly stable. Features and refactors can then be pulled strictly on-demand when the actual primary user asks for them.

### Real tradeoff tension
The plan fails to resolve the tension between **Architecture Coherence** and the **Lack of Game Unit Tests**. The audit explicitly stated there are *zero* unit tests for the 14 games. Yet, the plan schedules a massive Router migration (Phase 3b) and GameLayout standardization (Phase 3.1) across all of them. The hidden cost here is immense manual QA overhead. You cannot safely execute sweeping architectural changes across 13 untested games in "small, reversible" weekend PRs without either introducing subtle regressions or spending 80% of your time manually tapping through every game on a phone. The plan pretends these refactors are safe because the PRs are labeled "small," but the blast radius of a root router swap in an untested hub is inherently unsafe.

### Synthesis proposal
To resolve this tension, invert the sprint priority: deliver user value first, and gate the architecture work behind test coverage. Sequence the work as: CI Fixes (Phase 0) → Shipped Blockers (Phase 2) → Kid-Facing Polish (Phase 4a) → Drawing Identity (Phase 1). Move the Router migration (Phase 3b) and Vite upgrades (Phase 5) to the very end of the sprint. Before executing the Router migration, mandate the creation of a programmatic Playwright smoke test that loops through the game registry, loads every game, and clicks "Home" to automate the QA burden.

### Principle violations
*   **Principle 1 (Restore trust before features):** Violated by sequencing Phase 1 (adding a new Drawing Gallery feature) *before* Phase 2 (fixing the JellyVolleyball unplayable Blocker). Shipped broken code must be fixed before writing new feature code.
*   **Principle 2 (Small reversible PRs):** Violated by PR-3b (Router migration). The plan suggests feature-flagging the new router. You cannot safely feature-flag React Router hooks (`useNavigate`) inside leaf game components while falling back to a `useState` router; the hooks will throw runtime errors if rendered outside a `<Router>` context. Attempting to build a safe fallback bridge for this will create a massive, tangled, unreviewable diff.
*   **Principle 5 (Honor the primary user):** Violated by prioritizing Vite 6 upgrades and React Router (invisible to the user) weeks ahead of Phase 4a (pictographic difficulty selectors and win modals, which directly impact a 4-year-old's ability to play and enjoy the app).

### Sequencing concerns
*   **Phase 2 before Phase 1:** Blockers (JellyVolleyball touch) must be fixed before adding new features (Drawing Gallery).
*   **Phase 4a before Phase 3/5:** Kid-facing UX polish (Phase 4a) requires no major architectural changes and delivers immediate value to the child. It should be pulled forward to Week 2.
*   **Phase 3.4 (LocalStorage prefix):** Moving this into PR-1a makes PR-1a both a feature PR and a global data-migration PR. This mixes concerns. Run the storage migration as its own isolated PR *before* PR-1a.
*   **Phase 3.1 (GameLayout) after 3b (Router):** Standardizing the game layouts *before* swapping the router reduces the number of disparate `navigate` implementations the router PR has to hunt down and fix. 

### Blast-radius concerns
*   **PR-3b (Router Migration):** Touching the root `App.tsx`, the `HomePage.tsx` monolith, and 13 individual game components in one PR is too large. This needs to be split: PR1 creates the `registry.ts` and refactors `HomePage` to use it (data-driven UI), PR2 standardizes the GameLayouts, and PR3 actually introduces `react-router-dom`.
*   **PR-4a (Kid-facing polish):** Bundling Undo/Redo (complex canvas state array management), Sudoku hints (complex game logic), Win modals, AND First-run onboarding into a single "~3 day" PR is wildly optimistic. Undo/Redo is notoriously edge-case heavy and warrants its own PR entirely.

### Test/verify gaps
*   **Phase 1 PR-1a (Drawing save):** "Quota-exceeded path tested manually." This is highly prone to regression. It needs a Vitest unit test that mocks `localStorage.setItem` to throw a `DOMException` (QuotaExceededError) to prove the graceful degradation works.
*   **Phase 3b (Router):** Relying on a "manual checklist" to verify 13 games navigate home safely after a root router swap is brittle and exhausting.
*   **Phase 4d (Mobile layout):** Viewport-relative game sizing acceptance criteria are missing. Objective metrics (e.g., verifying canvas width does not exceed `window.innerWidth` via Playwright) are needed to prove it isn't broken on smaller screens.

### The one thing
Move Phase 2 (Blockers) and Phase 4a (Kid-facing polish) immediately after Phase 0 to deliver tangible value to the 4-year-old in Week 1, and push the high-risk Router/Vite refactors to the end of the sprint where they are gated by automated Playwright smoke tests.

### Verdict
REVISE_THEN_RECHECK

content.text:
Here's a tight reference based on what we just validated this session. Drop it in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or a personal cheatsheet.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The single non-obvious thing: **`--add-dir` requires `--dangerously-skip-permissions` in `-p` mode** or agy hangs forever with no output, no error, and no exit code. The harness has no way to detect that. This is why we lost the first architect run silently.
- The output is clean (no preamble like "Sure! Here's the answer:") which makes agy genuinely composable with shell pipelines — unlike some other CLIs that wrap everything in chat boilerplate you have to grep out.
- `agy` *is* the antigravity CLI — the name is just a contraction. Same model lineage as Google's antigravity work; closer in shape to `claude -p` than to bare `gemini -p`.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Raw agy command reference

### 1. Minimal one-shot (no file access)
```bash
agy -p "your prompt here"
```
Works out of the box. Returns the response on stdout with no preamble. Good for: pure-text reasoning, no codebase needed, fits in a single arg.

### 2. With workspace / file access ★ (the one that bit us)
```bash
agy -p "your prompt that references files" \
    --add-dir /path/to/project \
    --dangerously-skip-permissions \
    --print-timeout 10m
```
**The two flags that matter together:**
- `--add-dir` — mounts that directory into agy's tool sandbox so its Read/Grep/etc. can access it. Repeatable.
- `--dangerously-skip-permissions` — auto-approves the file-tool permission prompts. **Without this, `-p` mode hangs forever** because there's no TTY to confirm permissions interactively.

Skip `--print-timeout` and it defaults to 5m, which is too short for plans/reviews over a few hundred lines.

### 3. Long multi-line prompts (heredoc pattern)
```bash
agy -p "$(cat <<'PROMPT'
You are acting as ARCHITECT.

Read these files:
- /path/to/plan.md
- /path/to/spec.md

Return verdict + 3 paragraphs of critique.
PROMPT
)" --add-dir /path/to/project --dangerously-skip-permissions --print-timeout 10m
```
The `'PROMPT'` (single-quoted) heredoc preserves `$variables` literally — useful when your prompt contains shell metacharacters.

### 4. Continue a conversation
```bash
agy -p "follow-up question" --continue   # or -c
```
Resumes the most recent agy session. Useful for "now elaborate on point 2" without re-pasting context.

```bash
agy -p "follow-up" --conversation <id>
```
Resume a specific conversation by ID (from agy's session log).

### 5. Piping stdin (for big context that doesn't fit in args)
```bash
cat huge_file.md | agy -p "Summarize this in 5 bullets"
```
stdin is appended to the prompt. Works without `--add-dir` if you can fit the content via pipe.

### 6. Background usage (Claude Code / shell harness)
```bash
agy -p "..." --add-dir /path --dangerously-skip-permissions --print-timeout 10m &
```
Or inside Claude Code: pass `run_in_background: true` on the Bash tool call. The clean stdout makes the output file trivially `Read`-able.

---

### Gotchas to remember

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 0-byte output file, no exit, no error | `--add-dir` without `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Add the skip-permissions flag |
| Truncated mid-thought | `--print-timeout` exceeded | Raise to `15m` or `20m`; default is 5m |
| `command not found: agy` | Not on PATH | `/Users/yp/.local/bin/agy` is the install path; add to `$PATH` |
| Stale answer references wrong project state | agy injected a memory dump or pre-context | Check the first ~100 lines of output for an injected `## memory` block; ignore for analysis; agy 1.0.0 does this with claude-mem-style hooks |

---

### When to reach for agy vs gemini vs claude

| Tool | Best for | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|
| `agy -p` | Independent second opinion; clean stdout for shell composition; sandbox-mode reviews | Permission flag, memory-dump pre-context |
| `gemini -p` | Independent third opinion; broad knowledge; long-form synthesis | Occasionally returns `API returned invalid content` retry errors mid-stream (still completes) |
| `claude -p` | When you want the same model family as the orchestrator (consistency) | Cost; risk of self-confirmation if used as own critic |

---

### One-liner cheat for `/ralplan` and other consensus loops

```bash
# Architect/critic pass with workspace access:
agy -p "$(cat prompt.md)" --add-dir "$PWD" --dangerously-skip-permissions --print-timeout 10m
```

content.content:
## Architect Review — Plan v1

### Steelman antithesis
Option C ("surgical blockers only, then stop") is the strongest path forward, despite the planner's dismissive categorization of it as an "emergency exit" that "violates planning rigor." This is a dormant, single-developer hobby project with a strict 6-week window, built exclusively for the developer's 4-to-8-year-old daughter. The planner's recommended Option A—a 6-week phased marathon containing over 30 distinct items, framework migrations, major dependency upgrades, and deep-linking routers—is a textbook case of over-engineering. It behaves as though this codebase were an enterprise SaaS product with a team of active maintainers, rather than a dad writing game code for his child on weekends.

By adopting Option C, the developer secures a clear win on what actually matters. In a single weekend, the developer can fix the red unit tests (Phase 0.1), fix the broken touch coordinates on JellyVolleyball (Phase 2.1), and replace the drawing save console stub with a simple localStorage array (Phase 1.1). At that point, the application is fully functional, honest, and robust for the target audience. The kid does not care if the Sudoku page uses React Router deep-linking, if the dev-server runs on Vite 6 instead of Vite 5, or if the key namespacing has a schema migration shim. She just wants to draw, save her stencils, and play volleyball on her dad's phone.

Option A introduces massive, unmitigated execution risk. A single developer working only a few hours during evenings and weekends is highly susceptible to momentum loss. If the developer encounters a subtle routing defect on React Router v6 deep-links, an ESM configuration issue during the Vite 6 upgrade, or a test-environment discrepancy in Vitest 3, the project will easily stall. Option A is highly likely to end in developer burnout, leaving the codebase in a half-migrated, completely broken state. Option C protects against this failure mode by keeping the scope surgically small and immediately valuable.

### Real tradeoff tension
The single tradeoff not adequately resolved is the tension between **Technical Debt Remediation (Code Quality/Longevity)** and **Developer Delivery Momentum (Burnout Mitigation)**. 

The planner has prioritized academic code cleanliness (standardizing all 13 games on a single router, migrating 5 games to `GameLayout` to eliminate a few dozen duplicate lines of HTML header, namespacing keys, rewriting a working hook using `useReducer`) under the guise of "restoring trust" and "architecture coherence." However, in a solo hobbyist context, every hour spent refactoring working code is an hour stolen from implementing kid-facing delights (like sound effects, win animations, or drawing stencils) or spent increasing the probability of project abandonment. The plan fails to justify why the developer should spend valuable evening/weekend hours doing complex internal refactoring on a codebase that compiles perfectly and has zero active collaborators.

### Synthesis proposal
To resolve this tension, we should synthesize Option A's structural improvements with Option C's extreme focus on developer momentum. We can achieve this through a "Surgically Hardened Hybrid" approach:
1. **Promote the Blockers**: Pull the JellyVolleyball touch coordinates fix (2.1) and the localStorage drawing save loop (1.1, 1.3) directly into Phase 0/1. Do not make the kid wait weeks for a playable game.
2. **De-escalate the Refactors**: Drop the React Router v6 migration (3.2 / Phase 3b) and the `useReducer`/rAF rewrites (3.6, 3.7). ## RALPLAN-DR Summary v2

### Principles (unchanged from v1)
1. **Restore trust before adding features.**
2. **Small, reversible PRs.**
3. **One blast-radius-large refactor at a time.**
4. **Defer scope, don't expand it.**
5. **Honor the primary user** (the 4-8yo, not the developer's perfectionism).

### Decision Drivers (refined post-consensus)
1. **Visible value to the kid, fast.** Drives blockers-first sequencing and deferral of invisible refactors.
2. **Unambiguous fault attribution.** Drives deps-first so future bugs are clearly in new code, not new toolchain.
3. **Scope-collapsibility at any phase boundary.** Drives the new exit markers and the cancellation of low-ROI work.

### Options reconsidered

**Option A1 (this plan): Sequential phased sprint, scope-cut version**
Phases 0 → 6 below, with router migration cancelled and Vite upgrade pulled in. ~4 weeks at evening/weekend pace. Each phase has a clean exit.
*Pros:* Each phase ships value visible to a 4-yo. Scope-cuts the highest-risk work entirely. Survives partial completion.
*Cons:* Browser back-button doesn't work post-sprint. (Mitigation: rarely matters for an installed PWA / kids' app.)

**Option B (v1's plan): Original sequence with router migration kept**
Rejected by owner after architect divergence. Recorded for history. Would add ~1 week and high-blast-radius PR with marginal user-visible benefit.

**Option C (steelman, "blockers-only and stop"):**
Reaffirmed as the emergency-exit collapse path. At ANY phase boundary in this plan, owner may declare "scope-collapse here," and v2 is structured so the repo is in a known good state with no half-finished work. See "Scope-collapse exits" section below.

---

## Pre-Execution Identity Gate (unchanged)

Owner must affirm **Option B "kids' learning hub"** identity before Phase 2 (drawing identity work). Default assumption: B.

If owner picks A (re-focus on drawing) — Phase 4 expands to add stencil-system polish; Phase 6 (variety) becomes "drawing variety only"; defer game work to maintenance.
If owner picks C (split apps) — this plan is wrong; rescope.

---

## Execution Plan v2

### Phase 0 — CI honesty + regression net + storage shim (PR-0a, PR-0b, PR-0c, ~2 days)
